papers.title_en: Mask2Shield: Strengthening LLM Safety against Neuron-Pruning Attacks
papers.authors: Ying JinCheng, Minghui Xu, Yinhao Xiao, Xiuzhen Cheng, Wencheng Yang
papers.evidence: 掩码前向对齐方法降低对可移除安全神经元集的依赖以抵御剪枝攻击
papers.tldr: 大语言模型虽经安全对齐，但神经元级剪枝攻击可通过移除少量关键单元破坏其拒绝机制，同时保留模型可用性。为此，本文提出Mask2Shield（M2S）掩码前向对齐方法，训练掩码学生模型利用剩余计算恢复安全拒绝，并由冻结的无掩码教师提供正常回答以限制能力偏移。实验表明，M2S将313个提示下的成功剪枝攻击从80-279次降至1-44次，且基本保持模型能力。该工作有效降低了模型对少量可移除安全神经元的依赖，显著增强了LLM抗剪枝攻击的鲁棒性。
papers.abstract_en: Large language models (LLMs) are safety-aligned before deployment to reduce harmful content generation. Yet neuron-level pruning attacks show that refusal can depend on a small set of removable units: disabling them can remove safety behavior while leaving much of the model usable. To address this problem, we introduce Mask2Shield (M2S), a masked-forward alignment method that trains a model under this functional pruning. The masked student must recover a safe refusal through the remaining computation, while a frozen, unmasked teacher supplies complete benign answers to limit capability drift. Across ten model configurations, M2S reduces successful recomputed pruning attacks from 80--279 to 1--44 out of 313 prompts while generally preserving four capability benchmarks. We also evaluate M2S with TwinBreak, which uses a different neuron-selection rule and iterative pruning procedure. Together, these results show that M2S makes targeted pruning less effective by reducing reliance on a small, removable safety-neuron set.

papers.title_en: A Classifier That Teaches Itself: Self-Improving, Frozen-gate Training (SIFT) for Dynamic Document Classification
papers.authors: Bogdan Raduta, Horia Velicu, Alexandru Preda, Serban Chiricescu
papers.evidence: 廉价SPLADE+LightGBM分类器将低置信样本升级至LLM裁判，级联审核架构
papers.tldr: 企业文档分类的瓶颈在于前置标注成本与模型自主重训的安全风险。本文提出SIFT框架，用廉价SPLADE+LightGBM管线处理高置信样本，仅将低置信样本交由LLM裁判并回写语料库，实现昂贵模型持续教导廉价模型。同时引入双部件冻结门控机制防止关键指标回归。该系统使标注边际成本趋零，让无人工干预的自主重训安全常态化。
papers.abstract_en: Document classification is a solved problem in the laboratory and an unsolved one in the enterprise. The blocker is rarely model architecture; it is the labeling project that must precede a model and the institutional fear of letting a model retrain itself once one exists. We present SIFT (Self-Improving, Frozen-gate Training), a dynamic classifier service, which attacks both. SIFT serves classification from a deliberately cheap, CPU-bound pipeline, a SPLADE sparse encoder feeding a LightGBM head, and escalates only the low-confidence minority of pages to an LLM judge. The judge's verdicts are written back into a labeled corpus, so the expensive model continuously teaches the cheap one: the escalation rate falls, the corpus grows from production traffic rather than from an up-front annotation effort, and accuracy compounds with use. Onboarding a new document family requires only a declarative bundle, label space, anchor phrases, and a judge glossary, not a labeling project. The harder problem is safety: an autonomously retraining classifier can silently regress. SIFT resolves this with a two-part promote gate, a critical-label F1 regression check plus a frozen golden regression set the model is never trained on, either of which vetoes promotion. This turns "retrain monthly without a human" from reckless into routine. We describe the architecture, the self-feeding corpus loop, the frozen-gate promotion mechanism, and an illustrative multi-domain deployment, and we discuss the economics of a classifier whose marginal labeling cost trends toward zero.

papers.title_en: Beyond a Global Norm: Personalizing Toxicity Sensitivity in Language Models Without Retraining
papers.authors: Rares A. C. Diaconescu, Iulia Slanina, Alina Florea, Andrei B. Trache, Miruna E. Coroi, Anne Arzberger, Jie Yang, Enrico Liscio
papers.evidence: 无需训练的方法将语言生成对齐到用户特定的毒性敏感度
papers.tldr: 降低语言模型毒性常被视为全局对齐问题，但有害语言的感知因人而异。本文首次系统比较了无需重训练的推理时干预方法，以实现毒性敏感度的个性化对齐。实验基于PRISM数据集，所有方法均降低28-47%的对齐误差。研究揭示了有效性、个性化与语言质量间的根本权衡，证明该问题本质上是多目标优化。
papers.abstract_en: Reducing toxicity is often framed as a global alignment problem, yet perceptions of harmful language are subjective and context-dependent. We present the first comparative evaluation of training-free methods for aligning language generation to user-specific toxicity sensitivities across three inference-time intervention stages: pre-decoding (prompt conditioning and rewriting), in-decoding (token, logit, and representation steering), and post-decoding (candidate re-ranking). Evaluated against toxicity sensitivity targets derived from the PRISM dataset, all methods reduce alignment error by 28-47%. However, the results reveal a fundamental trade-off between alignment effectiveness, personalization, and general language quality, showing how toxicity sensitivity alignment is an inherently multi-objective problem.

papers.title_en: A Dual-Hypothesis Reasoning Framework for LLM Guardrails
papers.evidence: 使用LoRA参数高效微调和自生成策略的LLM安全护栏
papers.tldr: 现有LLM护栏在推理时易忽略提示的安全歧义，且依赖昂贵的大模型生成推理轨迹与全参微调。本文提出ARBITER框架，引入双假设推理显式对比安全与不安全解释，并结合多组件监督微调MC-SFT分解输出逻辑。该方法采用自生成策略与LoRA高效微调，在三个基准上超越现有基线，尤其在域外评估中优势明显，为LLM提供了低成本、高透明且可解释的安全护栏方案。
papers.abstract_en: We propose ARBITER, a novel LLM guardrail framework that introduces two key ideas: (i) dual-hypothesis reasoning, a reasoning method for LLM guardrails that explicitly considers both safe and unsafe interpretations of a prompt before making a safety decision, and (ii) multi-component supervised fine-tuning (MC-SFT), a structured training loss for reasoning-based guardrails that decomposes LLM outputs into logical components and weights them according to their importance. Existing reasoning-based guardrails often rely on expensive procedures, such as generating reasoning traces using larger or closed-source teacher models and applying full-parameter fine-tuning. In contrast, ARBITER uses a cost-effective self-generation strategy for reasoning traces and LoRA-based parameter-efficient fine-tuning while still achieving better performance than these expensive approaches. Additionally, ARBITER provides faithful evidence-phrase explanations for unsafe decisions, enabling a more transparent and interpretable guardrail method. Experiments on three safety moderation benchmarks show that ARBITER outperforms existing reasoning-based and non-reasoning guardrail baselines, with clear gains in out-of-domain evaluations.

papers.title_en: When Words Are Safe But Actions Kill: Probing Physical Danger Beyond Text Safety in Hidden-State Risk Space
papers.authors: Weimeng Wang, Ziqiang Wang, Zihang Zhan, Chuanpu Fu, Qi Li, Ke Xu
papers.evidence: 用于LLM安全分类的单层L2正则逻辑探针，低误报率
papers.tldr: LLM作为具身智能体规划器时，文本安全的指令在物理世界可能引发危险。本文探究发现内容危险与物理危险在LLM表征中是可分离的信号，据此提出单层L2正则化逻辑探针PRISM。PRISM在SafeAgentBench上达86.2-87.7%准确率且误拒率远低于LLM评判器，在无直接伤害词的PSB-1K上达99.6%准确率。本研究为超越文本审核的物理安全提供了表征级检测新范式。
papers.abstract_en: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly serve as high-level planners for embodied agents, where linguistically benign instructions can become unsafe once grounded in the physical world. We study whether this physically grounded danger is the same safety problem as ordinary text-level content danger. Through hidden-state direction analysis and random-split null tests, we show that content danger (CD) and physical danger (PD) form separable signals in LLM representations across Qwen2.5-3B/7B/14B/32B, Phi-3.5 and SmolLM2. Building on the CD/PD separability, we propose PRISM, a single-layer L2-regularized logistic probe over full hidden states. PRISM achieves 86.2--87.7\% accuracy on SafeAgentBench with 11.7--13.7\% FPR, while same-scale LLM judges over-block safe tasks at 24.7--39.0\% FPR. We further introduce PhysicalSafetyBench-1K (PSB-1K), a contrastive benchmark of 1{,}000 physical-risk pairs without direct harm keywords, to test whether methods detect physically grounded danger rather than explicit unsafe wording. On PSB-1K, PRISM reaches 99.6\% accuracy and 0.7\% FPR, whereas a Qwen2.5-3B judge rejects 67.8\% of safe tasks. PRISM also replicates on SafeText and EARBench, supporting hidden-state probing as a representation-level method for physical safety beyond text moderation.

papers.title_en: Conditional Reliability of Toxicity Signals for Multilingual and Code-Mixed Abuse Detection
papers.authors: Indraveni Chebolu, Rohan Singh, Arnab Mallick, Harmesh Rana
papers.evidence: ToxGate信任融合头用于滥用检测，对毒性信号进行条件门控
papers.tldr: 现有审核系统依赖的外部毒性工具在语码转换、音译和语言不匹配时极不可靠。本文提出ToxGate信任融合头，将外部毒性先验信号依条件于编码器表示后再融入预测。实验表明，ToxGate在12个域内设置中10个及8个迁移设置中7个取得提升，在高风险审核切片上增益最大且具可解释性。该工作表明应将外部毒性工具视为条件证据而非固定特征。
papers.abstract_en: Moderation systems increasingly rely on external toxicity tools, but those tools are unreliable under code-mixing, transliteration, slang, and language mismatch. We study the \emph{conditional reliability} of toxicity priors in Indian multilingual and code-mixed short text: English toxicity, Indic abuse, and rule-based severity cues can be useful evidence, but only in some linguistic and abuse-severity contexts. We propose ToxGate, a trust-fusion head that conditions each auxiliary signal on the encoder representation before adding it to the prediction state. Across three short-text abuse datasets, four transformer encoders, and five seeds per setting, ToxGate improves over matched plain encoders in 10 of 12 in-domain settings and 7 of 8 transfer settings. The largest and most interpretable gains occur in high-risk moderation slices, including explicit slurs, violent threats, and cross-dataset transfer. The broader lesson is that moderation systems should treat external toxicity tools and priors as conditional evidence rather than fixed features or ground truth, in focused ablations, source-specific gating gives the strongest results in transfer, severe-abuse slices, and high-risk triage.

papers.title_en: Distribution-Specific Curvature Control with Finite-Sample Guarantees for Open-Weight Safety
papers.authors: Domenic Rosati, Ali Dadsetan, Hong Huang, Xijie Zeng, Hassan Chowdhry, Subhabrata Majumdar, Hassan Sajjad, Frank Rudzicz
papers.evidence: 通过谱变形防止开放权重安全护栏的有害微调
papers.tldr: 开放权重模型易受微调破坏安全防护，现有谱变形方法全局增大曲率会阻碍良性适应。本文提出HarmAlign，沿估计的对比激活子空间进行保函数谱变形，推导出有限样本保证的曲率下界并转化为条件收敛速率控制。实验表明该方法有效阻断多种有害微调及自适应攻击，同时保持良性任务可训练，为模型安全提供严格理论保证。
papers.abstract_en: A short fine-tuning run can undo the safety guards of an open-weight model---retraining a refusal-trained assistant to aid weapons development or produce hate speech. Preventing such harmful fine-tuning while retaining benign adaptability remains difficult: the only prior method with an explicit curvature certificate, spectral deformation, inflates curvature globally and thereby obstructs benign adaptation along with harmful adaptation. We propose HarmAlign, which applies function-preserving spectral deformation along a estimated contrastive activation subspace. We derive finite-sample bounds for the estimated subspace energy and the resulting local harmful-distribution curvature lower bound. A stability--progress dichotomy for constant-step gradient descent turns the certified curvature into conditional convergence-rate control. Empirically, within a fixed-architecture, finite-budget first-order threat model, HarmAlign blocks direct fine-tuning and three data- or objective-adaptive attacks across a hazardous-knowledge relearning setting and a harmful-assistance fine-tuning setting, while the protected benign tasks remain trainable. The block persists across the tested first-order optimizer variants over every attack checkpoint, and under out-of-distribution harmful fine-tuning, and it extends to important cases in our threat model: accidental safety degradation and emergent misalignment.

papers.title_en: When LLM Defenses Backfire: Characterizing Safety, Performance, and Cost Trade-offs
papers.authors: Tong Zhang, Zexin Li, Simin Chen, Yun Peng
papers.evidence: LLM越狱防御权衡：安全性、过度拒绝与推理成本
papers.tldr: 大模型越狱防御虽能提升安全性，但常损害模型效用并引入额外代价。本文按操作策略系统分类防御方法，从性能影响、过度拒绝和推理成本三维度评估权衡。发现防御极少提升下游能力，而是在安全与可用性间做取舍：规则型保性能，自反思型易过度拒绝，多轮型推理开销最大。为评估防御副作用提供基准，并为部署选型提供实用指导。
papers.abstract_en: Jailbreak defenses are essential for protecting large language models (LLMs), but they can also introduce secondary costs that weaken model utility. We present a systematic study of these defense trade-offs along three dimensions: performance impact, over-refusal on benign inputs, and inference cost. Rather than treating defenses as a single class, we organize them by operational strategy and examine how different strategies correlate with different side-effect profiles. Across state-of-the-art defense methods, widely used benchmark datasets, and representative open-source LLMs, we find that defenses rarely improve downstream capability, but instead vary in how they trade safety gains against usability and efficiency. In particular, rule-based defenses best preserve task performance, highly conservative self-reflective defenses often increase over-refusal, and multi-round defenses incur the largest runtime overhead. These results provide both a benchmark for evaluating defense side effects and practical guidance for selecting defenses under deployment constraints.
